민수기-22-1.title: 민수기 22장 1절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-1.exegesis: 34-35. The Lord said unto Moses, Fear him not-- a necessary encouragement, for Og's gigantic stature ( De 3:11 ) was calculated to inspire terror. He and all his were put to the sword.

민수기-22-2.title: 민수기 22장 2절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 22 Nu 22:1-20 . Balak's First Message for Balaam Refused. 1. Israel ... pitched in the plains of Moab-- so called from having formerly belonged to that people, though wrested from them by Sihon. It was a dry, sunken, desert region on the east of the Jordan valley, opposite Jericho.

민수기-22-3.title: 민수기 22장 3절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-3.exegesis: 2. Balak-- that is, "empty." Terrified ( De 2:25 ; Ex 15:15 ) at the approach of so vast a multitude and not daring to encounter them in the field, he resolved to secure their destruction by other means.

민수기-22-5.title: 민수기 22장 5절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-5.exegesis: 4. elders of Midian-- called kings ( Nu 31:8 ) and princes ( Jos 13:21 ). The Midianites, a distinct people on the southern frontier of Moab, united with them as confederates against Israel, their common enemy.

민수기-22-6.title: 민수기 22장 6절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-6.exegesis: 5. He sent messengers therefore unto Balaam-- that is, "lord" or "devourer" of people, a famous soothsayer ( Jos 13:22 ). son of Beor-- or, in the Chaldee form, Bosor--that is, "destruction." Pethor-- a city of Mesopotamia, situated on the Euphrates.

민수기-22-7.title: 민수기 22장 7절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-7.exegesis: 6. Come ... curse me this people-- Among the heathen an opinion prevailed that prayers for evil or curses would be heard by the unseen powers as well as prayers for good, when offered by a prophet or priest and accompanied by the use of certain rites. Many examples are found in the histories of the Greeks and Romans of whole armies being devoted to destruction, and they occur among the natives of India and other heathen countries still. In the Burmese war, magicians were employed to curse the British troops.

민수기-22-9.title: 민수기 22장 9절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-9.exegesis: 8-14. Lodge here this night, and I will bring you word again, as the Lord shall speak unto me, &c.-- God usually revealed His will in visions and dreams; and Balaam's birth and residence in Mesopotamia, where the remains of patriarchal religion still lingered, account for his knowledge of the true God. His real character has long been a subject of discussion. Some, judging from his language, have thought him a saint; others, looking to his conduct, have described him as an irreligious charlatan; and a third class consider him a novice in the faith, who had a fear of God, but who had not acquired power over his passions [Hengstenberg].

민수기-22-20.title: 민수기 22장 20절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-20.exegesis: 19-20. tarry ye also here this night, that I may know what the Lord will say unto me more-- The divine will, as formerly declared, not being according to his desires, he hoped by a second request to bend it, as he had already bent his own conscience, to his ruling passions of pride and covetousness. The permission granted to Balaam is in accordance with the ordinary procedure of Providence. God often gives up men to follow the impulse of their own lusts; but there is no approval in thus leaving them to act at the prompting of their own wicked hearts ( Jos 13:27 ).

민수기-22-22.exegesis: Nu 22:21-41 . The Journey. 21. Balaam ... saddled his ass-- probably one of the white sprightly animals which persons of rank were accustomed to ride. The saddle, as usually in the East, would be nothing more than a pad or his outer cloak.

민수기-22-23.title: 민수기 22장 23절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-23.exegesis: 22. God's anger was kindled because he went-- The displeasure arose partly from his neglecting the condition on which leave was granted him--namely, to wait till the princes of Moab "came to call him" [Nu 22:20], and because, through desire for "the wages of unrighteousness" [2Pe 2:15], he entertained the secret purpose of acting in opposition to the solemn charge of God.

민수기-22-25.title: 민수기 22장 25절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-25.exegesis: 24. the angel of the Lord stood in a path of the vineyards-- The roads which lead through fields and vineyards are so narrow that in most parts a man could not pass a beast without care and caution. A stone or mud fence flanks each side of these roads, to prevent the soil being washed off by the rains.

민수기-22-29.title: 민수기 22장 29절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-29.exegesis: 28. the Lord opened the mouth of the ass-- to utter, like a parrot, articulate sounds, without understanding them. That this was a visionary scene is a notion which seems inadmissible, because of the improbability of a vision being described as an actual occurrence in the middle of a plain history. Besides, the opening of the ass's mouth must have been an external act, and that, with the manifest tenor of Peter's language, strongly favors the literal view [2Pe 2:15, 16]. The absence of any surprise at such a phenomenon on the part of Balaam may be accounted for by his mind being wholly engrossed with the prospect of gain, which produced "the madness of the prophet" [2Pe 2:16]. "It was a miracle, wrought to humble his proud heart, which had to be first subjected in the school of an ass before he was brought to attend to the voice of God speaking by the angel" [Calvin].

민수기-22-35.title: 민수기 22장 35절 역사문법적 주해
민수기-22-35.exegesis: 34-35. I have sinned ... if it displease thee, I will get me back again-- Notwithstanding this confession, he evinced no spirit of penitence, as he speaks of desisting only from the outward act. The words "go with the men" was a mere withdrawal of further restraint, but the terms in which leave was given are more absolute and peremptory than those in Nu 22:20 .
